text:
I recently had to attend a conference in Bialystok, but my university told me to keep in budget (spoilsports!). The suggested accommodation for the conference (several local hotels) were a bit pricey when I just needed somewhere to sleep, so I decided to try the Hostel Bialystok Centrum. My wife was a little worried by some reviews online, but I have slept in some pretty horrendous places, so decided to take my chance... I'm glad I did.

Arriving at Bialystok's recently modernised station (I remember it from 20 years ago, and it was grim... now it looks a lot better), I asked a taxi if he could take me to the hostel. He moaned that he would have to return all around a ring road and it wasn't worth his time for the trip. I asked how far it was and it was a pretty direct 15 minute walk, nothing complicated, "Just head for the big church!".

The entrance to the hostel is through a series of doors, requiring codes (which had been provided), and I managed to arrive before the receptionist finished work (10pm). The interior was clean and friendly looking. The lady welcomed me, showed me the room and the bathrooms (not en suite), the communal microwave and the kettle.

The bathrooms were clean and modern, which was a big relief. The nearest to me were 2 rooms which had a shower and toilet, and one room with a toilet. The shower was easy to use and had decent power and hot water. 

My double-bed room was small but perfectly fine for my needs. Even for two people, there was enough room (unless you are going to be dancing or doing acrobatics all over the place).

I ventured out for something to eat and found I was only ten minutes' walk from the rather nice city centre- plenty of pubs and fast food places, considering the hour.

Next morning, there was a knock at my door and the lady brought me breakfast (a surprise, as I thought I would be eating in some kind of dining room). Breakfast was basic- scrambled eggs, a hot-dog style sausage (parówka) and a plate full of freshly cut tomatoes, cucumber, salami and bread. I've eaten in a few hostels and hotels and this was quite a good breakfast for the price. Oh, and the lady asked whether I wanted tea or coffee (natural or instant), which she later delivered to the door.

I later asked for directions to the university, where the conference was, and the lady explained how to get there. It turned out to be the same road I'd walked the night before.

So, 3 nights (3-6 June) and no complaints. The staff were friendly and happy to help, and tolerant of my shoddy Polish.  All in all, a very pleasant surprise. 

The hostel also has traditional dorm style rooms with bunks.

Cost: 510 zlotych (around 120 pounds sterling,  $137, 120 euro).

Basic, clean, friendly, convenient and hot scrambled eggs. RECOMMEND.
title: A pleasant surprise

Stayed here for three nights and it ended up being exactly the kind of place you want for a city break. The location is hard to beat — right in the Old Town on Floriańska Street, so everything is within walking distance, but it still felt surprisingly calm once you were inside.

We had a Premium Suite which was properly spacious, not just “city hotel” spacious. Plenty of room to actually relax in the evenings rather than just sleep and go again the next day. The minibar was well stocked, bed was very comfortable, and the whole space felt clean, polished and easy to settle into.

The spa was a bit of a standout. Tucked away and really nicely done, and both times we went it was almost empty, which made it even better after long days walking the city. Exactly what you want when you’ve been out all day.

Nice touch with the prosecco on arrival, and the staff were consistently friendly and helpful without it ever feeling over the top.

We skipped breakfast as Krakow is far too good food-wise to stay in one place every morning, and I’d recommend doing the same — there’s so much to explore just outside the door.

Overall, it just made the whole trip feel easy. Would absolutely stay here again without hesitation.

I'm usually hesitant about booking a hotel near a train station but so glad we did. This is a beautiful modern hotel in a great location across the road from the tram, train station, buses and a huge shopping centre. However it's just a short stroll into the old town. The tram outside also allows you to quickly get to the Jewish quarter with its many restaurants and bars. Regular train from the airport and very easy to get to sites outside the city. 

The room wasn't huge, but was very well equipped with a great shower, a fridge, tea and coffee making facilities and a TV with inbuilt chromecast so you could cast netflix/youtube etc. Everything was spotlessly clean with a lovely modern European design. 

The bed was extremely comfortable. One of the best I've ever slept in, and comparable with beds in a 5 star hotel. Also amazing pillows. All controls (air con, lighting, alarm, menus) are via a tablet. 

Breakfast was excellent and well worth booking. Great coffee, a small menu of items that can be ordered (Shakshouka, avocado toast) and a buffet of juices, fruit, salad,  meat and cheese, bacon, sausage, scrambled eggs etc. All very good quality and regularly restocked. 

Staff were absolutely lovely and spoke perfect English. There's a small bar with a wide range of beers, wines and spirits. It's a little expensive, but it is a hotel bar I suppose! Oh, and there's unlimited free tea and coffee available in the lobby from an excellent bean to cup machine.

Kraków is an absolutely amazing city with so much to see and do. It's beautiful to walk around. It's also one of the cleanest cities I've ever been to. Everything in Poland seems to be done to a very high standard. Things just work and there's a real sense of optimism and order about the place. Of course, it is very touristy, and there are the usual CBD shops, overpriced restaurants in the square, and people with flyers trying to get you into a club/bar. However it's still a remarkable city and I will be back again. 

This is a really excellent hotel that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for convenience, facilities and extremely comfortable beds!

text:
My husband and I are huge fans of the Radisson Blu chain - they are always our hotel of choice, a home from home! 
We have just come back from 3 nights at the Radisson Blu in Krakow which was comfortable, clean and a great base for us during our trip. We love the little touches such as that welcoming “Radisson Blu scent” as you walk in to the lobby which instantly relaxes you, the friendly staff and cleanliness. We were checked in by Valentina who was very friendly and helpful and informed us that we had been placed in a Park View room which was lovely! 
We were very impressed with the sustainability efforts of the RB Krakow such as two sterile carafes in the room and a filtered water machine in the hallways for your unlimited use ensuring you always have access to cold, fresh, filtered water. Another lovely touch was that if you didn’t need clean towels etc then you hang a sustainable bag on your door handle which got filled with some little treats the next morning by housekeeping! We found this really lovely and actually looked forward to seeing what we got in there - it was like leaving a stocking out at Christmas! 
Some constructive criticism would be that we did not have any milk with our tea tray but this was soon put right once I asked a member of housekeeping on their rounds. The body wash container didn’t appear to have been topped up/ replaced before our stay which was a shame. I had luckily travelled with a mini body wash so we had an alternative but just something to stay on top of when more sustainable and refilling items as opposed to new bottles on the side that are more obvious. 
We found the room quite warm and the aircon was more of an air circulator than cooler which we both found very drying and would wake up with sore throats - this could only be turned off it the window was open but there was a sign to keep the windows shut after sunset due to bugs etc. The breakfast buffets were quite chaotic (the first morning it was a bit of a treasure hunt to find milk and a spoon) and you had to ask the staff for bacon which is usually something already out as part of the cooked selection but as it was all self service the staff were few and far between it wasn’t easily sourced.
That being said, our room was clean and comfortable, staff were friendly and the restaurant inside the hotel was great - tasty food and excellent service with friendly staff. We will continue to be top fans of the RB hotel chain and only wish they were in the locations we are heading to in Canada later in the year!!

text:
We visited Poznan with my parents in law for a family christening nearby.  We completed check in online in advance of arrival, so when we arrived to the hotel at about 1am, after delayed flight from Dublin, the process at the desk was super quick.  The girl was very welcoming and helpful also.  

We were in room 407, which was clean and spacious enough for our 4 night stay.  Shower was one of the best I've used in hotels to date.  Bathroom was also spotless and had hairdryer, box of toiletries (nail file, shower cap, cotton pads, cotton buds, shoe sponge, etc), towels, etc.  While bathroom walls were frosted glass, there was a thick curtain you could pull across bathroom wall / hallway to seperate the bed area, if required. Sufficient wardrobe space for two people.  Vanity table (although a large mirror here with better lighting would be useful.  Cans of still/sparkling water provided daily, as well as a mini fridge.  Digital panel in room for selecting areas of room to turn lights on.  Bed was comfortable with choice of two different pillows.  Duvet (duck feather I think?) was a little noisy the first night any time we moved, but we were so tired the nights that followed, that it didnt bother us.  

Breakfast was honestly the best I've ever had in a hotel!  There was a choice of four hot breakfast courses to order from the front of house staff member upon entrance (I had the poached egg and avocado toast each of the four mornings and was faultless each time!), but also other hot breakfast buffet, various dishes like salmon pate, herring in mustard mayo (my fave!!), tuna paste, etc.  Also cereals, granolas, fruit, meats, cheese, bread/rolls, salads, yoghurts.  Good quality coffee machines and delicious juices (try the cucumber / pineapple / ginger smoothie, so good!). 

We did not have dinner in the hotel, but popped in for a few beers / cocktails on two of the evenings - the Blackwater cocktail is delicious.  Breakfast staff / bar staff all very friendly and helpful and the general area is very comfortable.  

We joined the free 11am Saturday morning walking tour of the area - the tour guide was interesting to listen to and spoke clearly.  It gave us a great introduction to Poznan and was a lovely bonus with our stay.  

A coffee / hot chocolate machine is provided in the lobby, as well as a great selection of teas, along with fresh water.  There is plenty of comfortable couches / armchairs to relax in, as well as desk space if required.  

Location of the hotel was excellent - approximately 5 minute walk or less to Stary Rynek (main square) and other sites like Imperial Castle, Stary Browar (shopping centre) are all within wasy walking access.  The tram passes the hotel also, although we did not use public transport during our stay.  

We did however book taxis on two occasions through the hotel reception, both of which times they were there at the required time.  

There is a small gym on the fourth floor, as well as a sauna, but we did not get to use these.  

I would highly recommend Puro Hotel if staying in Poznan and would go as far as saying that based on our experience in their Poznan hotel, they would probably be a good choice if staying in any of the other cities where they are based.  I will definitely be considering them for future trips.

text:
I had to book a stay in Poznan for transit only hence the choice of hotel close to the train station. At the time I did not realise that I would be staying in a very historic hotel. It was interesting to read all about it in the lobby. Unexpected bonus to a nice stay.

The hotel is very modern. My room was incredibly spacious for one person. So was the bathroom. All spotless and bright. Brilliant idea to have water dispensers in the hall and a caraffe to fill with water yourself. I drink loads of water so this was welcome. Usually hotels leave one small bottle which I would drink in a minute and be left thirsty.

I was arriving very late so I asked if I could have a meal delivered to my room before the restaurant closes. I had to pay for it ahead of time using slightly confused process via email but it was worth it and the meal was very good. I also managed to grab a lovely glass of wine in the lively bar before they closed at midnight.

Breakfast, while pricey, was very good. Large selection of healthy and less-healthy foods - something for everyone. Offering was fresh and tasty. Coffee was nice and the service excellent.

All the staff across the hotel were friendly and helpful. The checkin and checkout was super easy. The proximity to the train station was a big plus for me. 

All in all 10/10 with a few caveats:

I was woken up by very loud music and shouting through microphone and speakers. It occurred later that it was Poznan Expo event nearby. Unfortunately I could not sleep after 8am which was disappointing becuase I really needed that rest. Not hotel's fault but I guess something to keep in mind.

The single beds seemed very narrow. I don't know if it was just me but I almost fell off the bed multiple times throughout the night.

Bar staff, while friendly enough, seemed tired and eager to close for the night. Maybe it was because of a large and loud group of guests at the time. But I didn't feel overly welcome.

The location was a bit odd. It is very close to old town and transport but immediate hotel surroundings are not particularly pleasant to look at. Felt deserted after dark.

text: The rooms here are surprisingly spacious, clean, and modern. The layout and design are also welcoming. The room I stayed in has a problem that is common in this Ibis/Novotel places, which is that if they get warm during the day, it's really hard to get them cool enough at night. I visited during a cool but sunny week, and my room was always very warm by evening. With no A/C or fans, the only way to get the room cool enough for sleeping is opening the window, but even on the top half of the hotel, where I was, the street outside is so noisy that you can't sleep without earplugs, and one night I woke up thinking that the fire alarm was going off in my room--I pulled my earplugs out to discover it was just the sound of sirens on emergency vehicles in the street below! To be clear, I liked everything about this hotel (it's even right next to a large, convenient, contemporary indoor shopping mall) except for this problem with the heat/noise.

text:
We stayed at Novotel Poznań Centrum for the first time, but we’re very familiar with the Novotel brand — one of the main reasons we chose it was the underground parking. The parking area is quite small, so keep that in mind if you’re traveling by car. We were lucky to find one spot available in the afternoon, but space is definitely limited.

The hotel is connected to an Ibis hotel (part of the same group). From what I understand, Novotel rooms are located on the higher floors, which offer beautiful views over Poznań’s Old Town. The location is fantastic — right in the heart of the city and within walking distance of the Old Town. In the evenings, it’s lovely to take a stroll through the nearby park and charming streets. There are many cafés and restaurants around, and a large shopping mall is directly across the street.

Our room was not huge, but spacious enough, cozy, and comfortable. Everything was spotlessly clean and well maintained. Breakfast was excellent — everything fresh, tasty, and with a great variety. The only thing we found a bit unusual was the location of the waffle makers and pancake station — they were in a separate room, which was slightly inconvenient, but not a big issue. The waffles we made were delicious!

Overall, we enjoyed our stay very much, and on our next trip to Poznań we will definitely consider coming back to this hotel.

text:
I stayed here for one night in early December. In truth I didn’t need a large trendy room as it was just a base for going out in the evening with some friends.

I was upgraded to a room with a balcony which was nice, but a balcony in December in Poland is of little use unless you are a smoker. The balconies all seemed to face inwards as well an overlook each other. Not a problem, just an observation.

My room itself was a decent size and the welcome chocolates as an acknowledgement of status were gratefully received. Unfortunately my stay was hampered due to the shower which wasn’t properly operational. Yes, water came out and yes, I could clean myself, but I only discovered this in the morning and had I been staying for another night I would have asked for another room.

Breakfast seemed quite chaotic (it was a Sunday morning though) and didn’t have a massive amount of choice. Although I had breakfast included, there didn’t appear to be anyone checking who did and didn’t have breakfast included, so maybe it is available to everyone. 

Checking out was also tricky as there was a large queue and no express check out box. There was only one member of staff trying to deal with everyone, so maybe the hotel was short on staff that morning. In the end I was out of time and had to leave my key on the side and didn’t manage to report the shower problem, which I would like to have done.

The hotel location is okay and not far from the centre, but does require you to cross a large main road if you want to walk to the Old Town. Cross with care.

This hotel is fine, but I wouldn't rush to stay here again.

For us, this was the most disappointing experience we’ve ever had in a Scandic hotel.

Upon arrival (around 2 PM) there was no warm welcome at all. We were told the room was ready, but immediately charged PLN 80 for an early check‑in — something we’ve never encountered anywhere in the world for a room that was already available. Even bringing our luggage to the room and leaving again would have cost the same. No discussion, no goodwill: “this is our policy”.

The next afternoon we were told by phone to vacate the room within fifteen minutes due to a water issue. We were moved to a larger but less practical room, but for just a few more hours this was hardly an improvement. The communication was blunt, and no gesture of compensation (not even a coffee) was offered.

The location near the station is convenient, but only if you have a room at the back. At the front, noise from traffic and trains is significant — even freight trains at 5 AM on a Sunday.

The restaurant felt gloomy and empty at dinner, but the breakfast buffet was excellent.

At check‑out, no one asked whether our stay had been satisfactory. We returned the key and received nothing more than an “OK”.

For us, this was definitely the last time here. There are many better and friendlier hotels in the area.

text:
If you’re looking for a hotel with real soul, the Sofitel Grand Sopot has it in spades. Walking up to this Grand Old Lady, you can feel the history settle around you right away. She’s elegant, she’s storied, and she’s definitely earned a few character lines, and I mean that in the best way. The fun part is knowing she’s about to get a serious facelift, inside and out, and you can almost feel the anticipation.

What absolutely made the stay unforgettable was the staff. Everyone I met seemed genuinely proud to be part of the place, and it shows. I have to call out Lukas, who was just exceptional. He brings so much warmth and professionalism that you instantly feel welcome. If the hotel itself has heart, he’s part of the reason.

Being there feels like stepping into a little pocket of Sopot’s history. The building, the atmosphere, the details, it all draws you in.

There’s also a historical tour that isn’t widely advertised. If you’re lucky enough to catch it, especially if you love history, don’t miss it. The hotel has seen some extraordinary moments, including visits from figures connected to the lead-up to WWII. Standing in the same spaces gives the whole stay another layer of meaning.

As for what I didn’t like? Honestly, nothing. Any small imperfections felt like they belonged to the story of the place, not flaws.

If you appreciate history, character, and truly excellent service, this hotel really delivers.

text:
A grand old hotel in a prime location right on the water. The property exudes historic charm, though the reception area and expansive hallways are in need of some attention — the carpet, for instance, is visibly buckled in several areas and detracts from the otherwise elegant atmosphere.

There’s a small bar just off the lobby leading into the grand dining room. We especially enjoyed relaxing with spritzes on the beautiful grounds that border the beach — a lovely setting for an afternoon break.

We arrived around noon, and reception kindly offered to notify us when our two rooms were ready, which she believed would be ahead of the standard check-in time. Unfortunately, we never received any update, and when we returned later, our keys were simply waiting on the counter.

We had booked Luxury Rooms (seaside view, two single beds combined as a king, no balcony). One room matched the representative photo from our confirmation, but the second was an attic-style room — quite possibly the least appealing room we’ve ever been offered. Thankfully, the staff quickly resolved the issue, upgrading us to a stunning oceanfront room and upgrading our traveling companion as well (also a perk - when available - of using our Travel Advisor).

There is a "strand" that parallels the ocean between the hotel and the beach, that was wonderful with restaurants scattered along the way in and around the various beach clubs. The charming Sopot downtown is also a short walk from the hotel, it was a great location for us.

The breakfast buffet was abundant and delicious, offering a wide variety of options. One disappointment, however, was the handling of the $100 credit per room we received through our Travel Advisor. At most hotels, this credit can be applied toward spa services, restaurant, bar, or even the final bill. At the Grand Hotel Sopot, it could only be used in the restaurant or bar — and all at once. Since breakfast was included, we didn’t dine in for lunch, and we preferred to explore local restaurants for dinner. Unfortunately, they had no way to debit the balance gradually (for example, with cocktails), so we ended up using the credit to purchase a $25 USD bottle of vodka for $200 USD — an unnecessarily restrictive policy that left a poor final impression.

text:
This remains an hotel with Grand aspirations.  Well-trained, charming staff; discreet décor and well-provided bedrooms.  The location is ideal, looking directly across neatly manicured private gardens to the beach and to the (very) long pier.  Also just a short walk from the commercial centre of the town.
Breakfast is a good, wide-ranging buffet in the restaurant.  We had two evening meals there two, which were not overwhelming however.  Disappointed that many, more local, guests don’t quite seem to grasp the concept of “smart casual”
One evening we were lured by a promise of Vivaldi to a recital in the concert hall.  However, the excellent vocal/instrumental quintet gave us a bit of Handel, Nessun Dorma, and a lot of Freddy Mercury/Queen stuff but no AV.
It appears that absolutely everybody who was a somebody has stayed in the Grand, and innumerable photos line the lounge walls.  I noted that a few better-known (but quite unspeakable) faces are omitted although Fidel Castro still clings on in the bottom left corner!
Reception and Concierge staff were very helpful with both suggestions on restaurants, an outing to Gdansk, and organising a private chauffeured tour of the Kasubia hinterland.
We didn’t try the pool or spa – these things are usually in an unpleasantly scented, humid basement.
But as a connoisseur of beaches, living ten minutes walk from the best sand in Cornwall, I can report that Sopot sand is fine, light golden, and (for a tideless sea) very clean.

text:
Stayed at the Radisson Blu Hotel in Sopot and the highlight by far was the (spa/sauna area) – what an amazing, refreshing wellness zone!
It’s textile-free inside (as expected for hygiene and proper sweating), and everyone is super respectful – men and women no problem, no staring, no awkwardness, just people chilling and enjoying the heat. There are a couple of great saunas: one hot/dry one and a milder one, plus a wonderful steam sauna that left me feeling fully refreshed.
The mixed-gender showers and changing areas with lockers worked perfectly – you can change privately if you want, but most people just use a towel to cover up when moving around, and it’s totally normal and no big deal. Just ask for a bathrobe and two large towels at the entrance (which they provide happily), and you’re set for the whole session.
I also booked a full-body massage (300 PLN) – excellent value! They give you a small disposable paper undie for modesty, so the therapist can work on your entire back, legs, etc., professionally and thoroughly. It was one of the best massages I’ve had – left me completely relaxed.
The hotel itself is lovely too: great breakfast selection (plenty of fresh options), comfortable rooms, and the whole place has a welcoming vibe. The spa access (60 minutes free per day for guests, easy to extend) made the stay even better.
If you’re open to the authentic mixed in-sauna experience this is a top spot in Sopot. Highly recommend – Will definitely return!

The bathroom was average with a sink, toilet and a shower. My daughter had her own room and hers looked similar like ours. Not sure if this is something new but if you wanted the room to be cleaned you had to ask for. It was no problem for us, we only stayed for 4 days.

We booked including breakfast and it was not a big buffet compared with other Hotels but a good one with all kinds of cold and warm meals and drinks and it was very nice. An extra point for us was, that we could enjoy our breakfast outside and could take our dog with us. 

The Hotel is close to the main street, which is going along the coast from Gdansk, Sopot, Gdynia up to Hel and therefore very convenient. I wouldn't call it myself the most quiet area due to the Street but it is still very calm.

What we didn't expect was the location itself. It is a 5 minutes walk to the beach and what was a fantastic positive experience. You walk 100 meters and end up in the middle of a beautiful park/woods, where you have stairs to get down to the beach. The park/woods contained bicycle track, inline-skating track and of course one for pedestrians.
The beach was not overcrowded and had a small Restaurant, where you could buy drinks and food, some installed umbrellas and as many people might not know, a dream of a beach. A dream, because it is wide, fine sand and clean.
Maybe the best feature was, that only 2 km. away is the "fun-mile" of Sopot, with Restaurants, some shops and entertainment. Because it is not far away, we walked every evening to the square, where the Marina lays and searched for a nice Restaurant.

In a nutshell. It was worth the trip, worth the money, good for a family and we enjoyed every minute spending there.
I don't think, you will regret it!

The bar area seems to be empty a lot and it's a bit soulless, but better to drink on the terrace. I was offered a welcome drink.

Ok, the apartment was nice. It was a studio though, not what we’d call an apartment. There is no door between bedroom and living room, and the bathroom door is glass (so no privacy). More annoying: no fridge. It’s the first time I have ever seen anything calling itself an apartment and yet have no fridge. That’s just not ok! Especially as trip advisor here says “all our apartments have fridge”. 

Comms were fine before the stay, and the location was great. Do not bother with taxis - bus 80 is very frequent - take it to Rondo Jagiellonow, change to any tram going towards old town - it’s one stop. There’s a 7-eleven (polish version) at the stop, and the street of the flat is just there, it’s a 3 minute walk. You can buy public transport tickets on machines across town, but the airport bus driver sells as well (it’s 3PLN for the ride across zones, or 60p. Why pay more? 

The apartment is less than 10 min walk to wild town, with the river and the boat rides, mill island and the tightrope Walker. Don’t miss the cathedral, it’s very pretty inside.

As the location is great for trans, don’t forget to use the trams down Gdanska street to visit the archer, the dancing fountain, the basilica and various museums.

text:
Let me start with an apology, if it was possible my rating would be 4.5 stars from 5.
I have very few concerns, and the ones I'm going to mention are more related to personal preference and not about any shortcomings with the hotel.
This hotel really must be a sliver away from being 4 star and I would suggest that it merits the upgrade.
Let's get the "bad" stuff over and done with first.
Despite being named the Novotel City Hotel, it's actually some distance from places of interest in the centre of Wroclaw. Certainly not walkable, and public transport is a ten to 15 minute walk from the hotel. With Bolt / Uber, it's easily remedied and at reasonable cost. It wouldn't stop me from staying here again.
My main gripe is actually related to something I am also passionate about. Protecting our natural resources. There's a few notices dotted around about water conservation. The room includes a refillable water bottle which I haven't seen at other hotels...a good thing. When it comes to the shower, their calculations might be a bit off!! They have some of the weakest water pressure I've ever experienced!! There's more water in the Atacama Desert in an average year than seems to be the case here!! I'm not asking to be blown off my feet, but come on, you can do better than what you have!!
My second and final concern is about the restaurant. It felt like I was at an airport hotel. You have the space to be so much more creative and interesting!!
Now to the good points...staff are generally warm and welcoming from assisting me with a restaurant booking on the night of my arrival to a late dinner at the hotel restaurant. I am grateful.
Room size is excellent...spacious and comfortable. My room overlooked a patio with large umbrellas, obviously this area could be used for functions and maybe as an extension to the bar. If in use, I would have been concerned as the rooms are not soundproofed.
The beds are comfortable, though the pillows were a little soft for me.
My room was very well maintained by the domestic team, absolutely spotless!!
I would be very happy to stay here again on my next visit.
Thanks to all for your efforts.

The rooms are delightfully rustic and comfortable with surprisingly high-speed internet (12 MB/s!), and absolutely silent all night. 
The food is a little idiosyncratic in that they serve a full meal at 2-4 in the afternoon and then a lighter buffet at night, though lots of choices and plenty to eat - smoked fish, quiche, pierogi. And of course a typical polish breakfast spread. The staff are pleasant but reserved. When we learnt that they don't take Visa on leaving, the owner said no problem at all - just wire the balance when you get home. She wasn't in the least concerned. There are dry sauna, wet sauna areas.  Very relaxing just to spend the time in each.  My wife and I used their spa services.  Again, high end, profesional, relaxing.  
Location is noteworthy.  Place is walking distance away from the train station.  It is also by the main passage that’s filled with restaurants and shops.  
Let’s talk about food.  Breakfast is an experience here.  Food items are high end, selected, premium.  I live half of my life at the world brand hotels and can speak with experience that the breakfast time here is above average.  That alone is worth the stay.
We have celebrated the New Year’s celebrations here at their venue.  The night left a lasting experience with my wife and our friends.  Chef had summoned raw fresh oysters for an appetizer.  There was lobster bisque.  Scallops were available.  Language was plentiful. Again, I’ve experienced Michelin style restaurants in New York and Singapore.  Zakopane and Aries Hotel will compete easily with them all. Yes, there was a steak.  So thick, it resembled a cube.  Bravo to chef.

text:
Fabulous hotel. 

We had a problem with our room but the staff did everything to sort it.  I had phoned them to enquire regarding rooms to sleep 2 adults and 2 children and was told that the sofa bed size in the aries suite and the grand aries suite were identical and only difference was the floor size.  I was reassured that in both the sofa bed would be plenty big enough for 2 children aged 8 and 10.  The room we were allocated on arrival had a tiny sofa bed in it, barely bigger than a single bed.  I immediately asked about availability of a roll-out bed (assuming they all had same sofa bed as I had been told) and was told this was not available that evening but they would try in the morning.  Kids had an uncomfortable night's sleep.  Next morning asked again and they said they would move our room.  The new room was of similar floor space but had a proper double sofa bed. Kids slept comfortably for the remaining 4 nights. 

Hotel immaculately clean.  Rooms well appointed. Decent showers.  Excellent breakfast, lots of choice and all very tasty.  Lovely pool area. Pool itself too cold for me but nice outdoor hot tubs. 

Location is great.  Just a few hundred metres from the main shopping street.  Its around a 25-30 minute walk to Snowlandia, probably 10 minutes to the funicular to Gublowka.  Free parking on site.  Car park slightly annoying as have to buzz each time and not answered particularly promptly. 

Staff all very helpful - advised on where to go sledging and other activities. 

Not the cheapest in the area but we very much enjoyed our stay and I would definitely go back if going back to Zakopane.

text:
A bit of trickery on the adverts on the booking website that we booked with there was a picture of a new detached style bungalow as a picture that we thought we were getting, as you can guess we did not, there are two such new bungalows at the hotel, but only two. 

We had an apartment in the main building right next door to the reception with a separate bedroom to the right as you enter with two single beds, a kitchen (that we never used), a beautiful bathroom with just a shower (no bath)  a large lounge with a table, TV, sofa and other furniture, and in the lounge was steps to a raised mezzanine bed area with a double bed.  The apartment was very large and looked beautiful, we were initially impressed by it.  The apartment was spotlessly clean. 

Then the HEALTH and SAFETY matters came to notice, on the raised mezzanine level with the double bed there are beautiful metal railings, but they DO NOT GO UP VERY HIGH, in fact I felt very uncomfortable sleeping up there as the railings were only slightly higher than the level of the bed.  Without much effort or cost an extra level of railings could be placed above the present ones that could remove this insecurity.  I certainly would not want to sleep on the mezzanine level if I was intoxicated there is a very real risk of one falling over the railings onto the floor below.  Our daughter could never sleep here as she sleep walks.  

Then there was the stairs leading to the mezzanine level, they are wooden and do not have any grip on them whatsoever.  You walk up and down them exceedingly carefully             as they are steep, we all told each other to be careful but on our last day one of our party slipped on the stairs and hurt themselves they had a bruise on their back the size of plate and swelling, and bruising on their buttocks.  The reception were told of this in Polish and the member of my family was told "No one has reported such an incident before", I do not think anything will be done about it.
We may not be young but we are not old and clumsy, we are all accomplished intermediate skiers and are quite agile so this in my opinion is a very real hazard. 

Sadly for us our beautiful looking but not safe apartment was right next door to the banqueting hall area where there is a bar and you eat breakfast.  We were there on a Saturday night when there was a beautiful wedding reception, well it was beautiful for the bride, groom and the guests, but not so beautiful for us who wanted to get to sleep. Anyone who knows about Polish weddings they go on until 06:00am or so with the young bucks and maidens energetically dancing away. 

This apartment should of been given to a member of the wedding party and us given their rooms, it would of been perfect for them the women could go quickly to get changed into their second dress of the night, and for the chaps a fresh shirt, as it was so close to the wedding reception.  A bit of poor forward thinking by the booking staff I am sure a large number of the guests at this wedding stayed the night. 

Breakfast was very good as was the two dinners we ate at the hotel. The hotel does a large platter made out of wood of meat or fish plus potatoes, salads and vegetables for very reasonable money it tastes good, but if you order individual meals each then the quality of the food is much better even if it is a little bit more expensive.  The waiter staff were well presented, polite and efficient.  Whatever you asked them they were happy to assist and dealt with requests promptly.  The bar staff were at times a bit slower we had to wait 30 mins for a hot chocolate for our daughter to drink before bed, despite me placing the order and questioning twice "where is the hot chocolate".   

There is a small beach with a roped off swimming area, sadly the roped off area is very small and the water level only comes up to just above ones waist, this does restrict your swimming and enjoyment of the lake.  There is no lifeguard at this beach.  The roped off area if possible should be extended and this would make swimming more enjoyable.

We  hired a canoe and went out onto the lake it was fun and great to see the wildlife, you had to pay extra for this, there was also a motorboat you could hire, but we did not fancy listening to the noise of an engine, plus it was not so cheap.   

There is also a beautiful sauna, steam room and shower that you need to book for free. They were also spotlessly clean and very very hot.
title: A nice hotel beautiful rooms, good food but some Health Safety worries, and other niggles

text:
This historic, well restored manor, originally built in 1830 gave us a lovely, relaxing experience. Both the exterior and the interior are nicely decorated. Since it was almost Christmas, the hotel was decorated with lights, Christmas trees, wreaths, etc. 

The staff is very accommodating and helpful. The manager could not have been kinder. She made sure that everything was just right during our stay. When we arrived the receptionist, who spoke English, escorted us to our room and made sure that everything was arranged as we would like and asked us what time we would like breakfast the next day.

We enjoyed the breakfast every morning included in the stay. It was a continental spread of meats, cheeses, breads, eggs, cucumbers, tomatoes, yogurt, cereal, orange juice, coffee, and tea.

Then, I enjoyed taking a walk in the park every day. Two large oak trees span across the long lawn. There is a gazebo, small pond, stream, walking trail through the trees, a pool, tennis court, three swings and a little garden in the back corner. After translating the signs, I discovered it includes blueberry bushes, cherry, apple and pear trees. The whole park was lovely in the winter as small wisps of snow came down. I am sure during the greener, warmer seasons of the year it is gorgeous as well.

The room had plenty of space with a small table, two chairs, a television and a very comfortable bed. Every day they put two bottles of water in the room. The bathroom had a nice, warm shower with toiletries waiting for us. The beautiful view from the two windows in our room overlooked the park behind the hotel. 

Two of the nights, we reserved the jacuzzi. It is included in the price. We reserved it that morning so they could have it warm and ready for us.  It was so nice in a room downstairs in the spa. They lit candles in the room and it was very special. 

We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and recommend the hotel highly.
